title: Behind the front, with Lijssenthoek
ring: History XL · Nine Elms · Talbot House · Lijssenthoek · {{KM}} km ·
sub: The town behind the Salient, and the biggest hospital cemetery of the war.
desc: A {{KM}} km walk from Kleine Dasdreef over Nine Elms, Talbot House, the death cells, Poperinghe New Military Cemetery and Lijssenthoek Military Cemetery.

waypoints.name: Home
waypoints.title: Out of the door
waypoints.note: Down the gravel lane to Kleine Dasdreef, then left, up the dreef to Helleketelweg and right, towards town.

waypoints.name: Nine Elms
waypoints.label: Nine Elms
waypoints.title: Nine Elms British Cemetery
waypoints.note: Ten minutes from the door, between the fields on Helleketelweg: 1,556 graves from the casualty clearing stations that stood here in 1917 and 1918. Among them Dave Gallaher, captain of the 1905 All Blacks, killed at Passchendaele.
waypoints.accent: Most people in Poperinge do not know it is here.

waypoints.name: Hopmuseum
waypoints.title: Into town by Werf and Gasthuisstraat
waypoints.note: Werf and Duinkerkestraat bring you into Gasthuisstraat, the street where the soldiers' Poperinge happened: cafés, shops, the Hopmuseum in the old weighing house, and halfway along, number 43.

waypoints.name: Talbot House
waypoints.label: Talbot House
waypoints.title: Talbot House
waypoints.note: The Everyman's Club opened by chaplains Tubby Clayton and Neville Talbot in December 1915, where rank was left at the door and the chapel was in the hop loft. Still a house, still open, still serving tea in the garden.
waypoints.accent: Open daily 10:00 to 17:30. Give it an hour if you go in.

waypoints.name: Dodencellen
waypoints.label: Death cells
waypoints.title: The death cells and the execution post
waypoints.note: In the courtyard behind the town hall on Grote Markt: the cells where condemned soldiers spent their last night, and the post against which they were shot at dawn. Free, quiet, and the hardest minutes of the walk.
waypoints.addr: Guido Gezellestraat 1, behind the town hall

waypoints.name: Pop New Mil Cem
waypoints.label: New Military Cemetery
waypoints.title: Poperinghe New Military Cemetery
waypoints.note: South-east of the centre on Deken De Bolaan. 677 Commonwealth and 270 French burials, and seventeen soldiers executed in the town; more than in any other cemetery of the war.

waypoints.name: Lijssenthoek centre
waypoints.title: South on Boescheepseweg
waypoints.note: Deken De Bolaan becomes Boescheepseweg and leaves town between the fields. Three kilometres later, on the right, the visitor centre of Lijssenthoek (free, open 9:00 to 18:00).

waypoints.name: Lijssenthoek
waypoints.label: Lijssenthoek
waypoints.title: Lijssenthoek Military Cemetery
waypoints.note: The hospital cemetery of the Salient: 10,784 graves beside the railway siding where the casualty clearing stations stood. Almost everyone here died in a hospital bed, not in battle. One woman among them, nurse Nellie Spindler.
waypoints.accent: The second largest Commonwealth cemetery in Belgium.

waypoints.name: Lyssenthoek
waypoints.title: West by the Lyssenthoek lane
waypoints.note: Leave the cemetery by the lane called Lyssenthoek, west through the fields to Abeelseweg; a short stretch on its cycle path, then right into Stoppelweg.

waypoints.name: Vijfgemetenstraat
waypoints.label: Vijfgemetenstraat
waypoints.title: Stoppelweg and Vijfgemetenstraat
waypoints.note: North past the edge of Helleketelbos, then right into Kleine Casseldreef.

waypoints.name: Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.label: Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.title: Home by Kleine Casseldreef
waypoints.note: The long straight lane back towards the dreef and the gravel lane.

goodtoknow: Pavement in town, lanes and a cycle path outside it. Everything is open around the clock except Talbot House (from 10:00), the death cells (closed Mondays) and the Lijssenthoek visitor centre (9:00 to 18:00). Allow extra time: this is a day with four stops worth lingering at.

Poperinge was never taken in the First World War. It sat eleven kilometres behind Ypres, out of range of most guns, and became the place where the soldiers of the Salient slept, drank, were patched up and, for a few, were shot.
more: Nine Elms was the cemetery of two casualty clearing stations, set up in the fields west of the town in September 1917 for the Passchendaele offensive. Talbot House took its name from Gilbert Talbot, killed at Hooge in 1915; his brother Neville founded the club with Philip Clayton, and the Toc H movement grew out of it after the war. The death cells and the execution post behind the town hall were restored and opened as a memorial; the New Military Cemetery holds seventeen of the men who died there.
tlcue: Clockwise. Distances are from the front door.
